messages.subject: Interpreting Occurrence distributions
parts:
Hi Chris, 

Struggling to interpret the occurrence distributions I have computed - I think its something simple that I've overlooked, but I thought I would ask cause think it is important.  

The occurrence distribution "specifies the probability that the animal occurred within an area at a randomly chosen time within the observation period" (Fleming 2016;). Makes sense. What I can't wrap my head around then is why the probabilities are the lowest where we are certain the animal went ( the known locations). I have attached a screenshot of an occurrence distribution shown with the trajectory points plotted.  You can see the probabilities are lowest where the known locations are.  What am I missing here?  

Thanks, Robin

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Interpreting Occurrence distributions
parts:
Hi Robin,

You probably exported the CDF, and so those values correspond to the percent coverage (0% - 100%), where 0% would be the mode and 100% is far from the data. Alternatively you can export the PDF or PMF: https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/reference/export.html

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Interpreting Occurrence distributions
parts:
Hi Robin,

The PDF is the probability density function or probability per unit area (with physical units of 1/meters^2). Maybe you want to export the probability mass function (PMF) which is the total probability mass in the cell (0-1). Note that you can only compare PMFs calculated with the same grid.

Best,
Chris
